name: Tuxedo
description: Tuxedo is a card-capturing game invented by George Parker, played with a 56-card Rook deck (no Rook card). 4 cards per player + 4 face-up in the 'pond'. Capture by matching number or matching sums. Sweeps (clearing the pond) score bonus. 'Orange' call bonus for capturing red+yellow together. First to 100 wins.

history.origins: Tuxedo is an American Casino variant often attributed to George Parker (Parker Brothers). It is played by 2 to 6 players using a Rook deck, with mechanics matching American or Royal Casino and distinct scoring: most cards, orange captures (red and yellow together), sweeps, and fives; first to 100 wins. The HOYLE Card Games collection includes a Tuxedo program.
timeline: Early 20th century: American Casino variant published by Parker Brothers, played with Rook deck.

setup.deck: 56-card Rook deck (no Rook card). 4 colors, values 1-14.
setup.dealing: 4 each + 4 face-up (pond). Redeal 4 when hands empty.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing cards (match number or sum to 14), sweeps, 5s, Orange call (red and yellow together), and most cards; first to 100 wins.
rules.gameplay: Play 1 card per turn. Capture matching number or cards summing to your card's value. Can't capture = play to pond. Sweeps: Big Sweep (4+ cards) = 10 pts. Little Sweep (3 or fewer) = 5 pts. Orange call: Red+Yellow captured = 10 bonus (must call 'Orange!'). 5-value cards = 5 pts each. Most cards = 15 pts.

strategy.basic: Capture high-value cards. Go for sweeps.
strategy.advanced: Track remaining values. Control the pond.

scoring.description: Most cards=15. Sweeps=5/10. 5s=5. Orange=10. First to 100.
